main_result.evidence: Compared with YOLOv8s and RT-DETR, mAP@.5 is improved by 3.3% and 1.4% respectively, while maintaining the reasoning speed better than RT-DETR.

coder_notes: NEU-DET was expanded via rotation, random cropping, and Gaussian noise before or with the 8:2 random split (total 3350 in Table 1), which explains the unusually high mAP@.5 (90.1% for YOLOv8s, 94.3% for MFDH-Net). In Experimental parameter settings, '300 iterations' and '300 rounds of loops' refer to 300 epochs (consistent with Fig. 14 and Fig. 21 showing up to 250-300 epochs).
